description: As ARGEM high school students for NASA Space Apps Adana, we focus on computer science, electronics, and physics. We are a disciplined team of 5 with strong communication. Offering great energy where your ideas matter, we are looking for teammates interested in software, hardware, data analysis, or presentations who can keep up with the hackathon pace!
summary:
We are developing a map-based decision-support tool that uses historical wheat-production zones and environmental data to estimate how climate change may shift suitable wheat-growing areas across North America. The tool will map these potential shifts and divide the areas along the projected routes into zones. A mathematical model will then compare crop-rotation options for each zone, considering economic value alongside factors such as soil health, water availability, and climate conditions. It will help farmers explore which crops to plant and when, year by year.

This addresses the challenge by turning Earth observation and agricultural data into practical, location-specific rotation options that farmers can compare. It is important because changing growing conditions may make established planting plans less suitable. By helping farmers plan ahead and weigh economic returns against soil and water needs, the tool aims to support more resilient and sustainable farming. Its recommendations are intended to inform farmers’ decisions, not replace local expertise.
details:
Our project is a map-based decision-support tool for wheat farmers in North America. It uses historical wheat-production zones and environmental data to estimate how climate change may shift areas suitable for wheat cultivation. The map divides these areas into zones along the projected shift. For each zone, a mathematical model compares crop-rotation options and identifies which crops and planting periods may offer the best balance of economic value, soil health, and water availability.

The tool is intended to help farmers anticipate changing growing conditions and plan their crops year by year. By comparing rotation options across zones, it can support more informed decisions, reduce uncertainty, and encourage farming practices that are both economically viable and resilient to climate and water challenges. We hope to show how Earth observations and agricultural data can be turned into practical recommendations for future wheat production. We developed our project in Python, JavaScript and HTML, using Leaflet and d3.js for the interactive map and charts. We used NASA POWER climate projections, MODIS satellite data, the USDA Cropland Data Layer and USDA NASS statistics. No special hardware was needed; everything runs on a standard laptop.
projectRefs: Commodity Costs and Returns - USDA ERS
